problem: Find the equation of the left-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(1,4)$ and passes through the point $(-1,8).$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Left or Right-Opening Parabola Given the Vertex and Another Point
examples.problem: Find the equation of the left-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(2,-2)$ and passes through the point $(-6,2).$
examples.worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h, k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h, k) = (2,-2),$ we substitute $h=2$ and $k=-2$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+2)^{2} & =4p(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(-6, 2),$ so we can substitute $x=-6$ and $y=2$ into the equation above and solve for $p\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+2)^{2} & =4p(x-2) \\ (2+2)^{2} & =4p(-6-2) \\ 16 & =-32p \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+2)^{2} & =4p(x-2) \\ (y+2)^{2} & =4(-\frac{1}{2})(x-2) \\ (y+2)^{2} & =-2(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13954664/assets/d4d0ad25fe8409b55ad4021c5e06d0f13579cea804b1a2b78b18b3ba76bd0c0e.png)

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
feedback.worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the right. The parabola has its vertex at $(-4,2)$ and passes through the point $(2,6).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(-4,2),$ we substitute $h=-4$ and $k=2$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x+4).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(2,6),$ so we can substitute $x=2$ and $y=6$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x+4) \\ (6-2)^{2} & =4p(2+4) \\ 16 & =24p \\ p & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x+4) \\ (y-2)^{2} & =4(\frac{2}{3})(x+4) \\ (y-2)^{2} & =\frac{8}{3}(x+4).\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since $p=\frac{2}{3}$ is positive.
